This petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act 1989 is filed seeking compensation for the death of Smt.S.Selvi W/o.Jaishankar in a road traffic accident.

2. It is stated in the petition that on 16-11-2023 at about 7-40 a.m. the deceased Selvi was traveling as a pillion rider on a motorcycle bearing No.KA-51-ET- 9016, ridden slowly and cautiously by her husband near Meenakshi Mall Junction, Bannerghatta main road, Bengaluru.

It is alleged that a private bus bearing No.KA-01-AA-4947 (herein after called as offending vehicle) came from behind,
in a rash and negligent manner and collided with the motorcycle.

Due to the impact, Selvi fell,
sustained grievous injuries and died on the spot.
Thereafter postmortem was conducted at St.John's Medical college hospital, Bengaluru and the body was handed over to the Petitioners.
3. The petitioners contend that the accident was solely due to negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
At the time of accident, the deceased was aged about 49 years, working as a Tailor and earning .25,000/- p.m.
The Petitioner No.1 to 3, being her husband, two daughters of the deceased, were depending on her income of deceased and have suffered mental shock, agony and loss of their bread winner.
An amount of .2,00,000/- was also incurred treatment, funeral and other expenses.
The petitioners have sought compensation of .50,00,000/- with interest from the Respondent No.1 and 2 being the insurer and insured of the offending vehicle.
4. In response to the petition notice, Respondent No.1 appeared through counsel and filed objections.
The respondent No.2 remained absent and was placed exparte.

5. The 1st Respondent - in its objection statement admitted the issuance of policy in favour of offending vehicle and its validity on the date of accident but stated that its liability is subject to terms and conditions of the said policy.

It denied that the allegation of negligence on the part of the offending vehicle and contended that the accident was caused due to negligence of the motorcyclist and the deceased, who allegedly not wearing a helmet at the time.
6. The respondent no 1 further contended that the owner of the offending vehicle and the concerned police have failed to comply with the mandatory provisions of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.

It also claimed that the driver of the offending vehicle was not having a valid driving licence and that the vehicle itself did not possess a valid fitness certificate or permit at the time of the accident.

The age occupation, and income of the deceased were also disputed and the compensation claimed was Jaishankar vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67611318/
2 termed as excessive and exorbitant, seeking dismissal of the claim.

sentences.text:
7. On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues have been framed :-
1.

Whether the petitioners prove that on 16- 11-2023 at about 7-40 a.m. near Meenakshi Mall Junction, Bannerghatta road, Bengaluru City, Selvi W/o.Jaishankar, the wife of petitioner No.1 and mother of petitioner No.2 and 3, sustained injuries in a road traffic accident, while she was a pillion rider in two wheeler number KA-51-ET-1916, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Private bus bearing number KA-01-AA-4947 and succumbed due to injuries on the spot?
2. Whether the respondent No.1 proves that the policy conditions are violated by respondent No.2 and the respondent No.1 is not liable to pay any compensation?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation? if any, how much, from whom?
4. What order or award ?
8. In support of their claim, 1st Petitioner is examined as PW.1 and got marked the documents as per Ex.P.1 to P.14.
9.
The respondent No.1 has examined the official of RTO, Bengaluru Central as RW-1 and got marked the documents at Ex.R.1 to5.

On the other hand, RTO of Bengaluru central was examined as RW1 and official of respondent No.1 is examined as RW-2 and got marked the documents at Ex.R.6 & 7.
10.
I heard the counsel on both sides and have perused the material on record.

11. By considering the evidence and materials available on record and after hearing the arguments my findings to the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative Issue No.2: In the negative Issue No.3: Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.4: As per the final order, for the following:
REASONS 12. ISSUE NO.1:- Petitioners say that on 16-11- 2023 at about 7-40 a.m. the deceased Selvi was travelling as a pillion rider on a motorcycle bearing No.KA-51-ET-9016, ridden slowly and cautiously by her husband near Meenakshi Mall Junction, Bannerghatta main road, Bengaluru.
It is alleged that a private bus bearing No.KA-01-AA-4947 (herein after called as offending vehicle) came from behind, in a rash and negligent manner and collided with the motorcycle.

Due to the impact,
Selvi fell, sustained grievous injuries and died on the spot.
Petitioners say that it was the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.

They relied on the police records and submitted that the police Jaishankar vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67611318/
3 have filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle and it is requested to award compensation from the owner and the insurer of the offending vehicle.

sentences.text:
13. In support of their version Petitioners have produced FIR, Complaint, PM report and inquest,
spot mahazar, IMV report, rough sketch and Charge sheet at Ex.P1 to 8.
14. To prove the negligence on the part driver of the offending vehicle, 1st Petitioner examined as PW- 1 and he relied on the police records.

Respondent- insurance company has denied petition averments and generally denied all the allegations made against the driver of the offending vehicle and denied rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending.
It is contended by the Respondent - insurance company that the accident occurred due to negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle.
15. The Respondent -insurance company has not placed any materials to disprove the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
During the course of cross-examination of PW1, learned counsel for the Respondent no 1 has suggested that the accident occurred head on collision.
However, this suggestion was specifically asserted by PW1, that the offending vehicle had struck the two wheeler from behind.
Further he denied that the two wheeler had sustained front damage.
In the absence of any substantive rebuttal or supporting evidence from the insurance company, the presumption of negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle remains unshaken.
16. All the materials clearly indicate that the accident was due to the negligence of driver of offending vehicle.
There is no material on record to disprove the PW1 evidence and to prove the contention of the Respondent no 1.
The evidence of PW-1 corroborate with the documents produced by PW1.
There is nothing elicited to disprove the case of the petitioners.
It is well settled principle that Motor Vehicles Act is beneficial legislation, the tribunal need not to go for the strict proof of rash and negligence.
Charge sheet prima-facie establishes the rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
From all the above documents it is clear that Selvi died in a road traffic accident that occurred only due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of offending vehicle.
Hence I answer Issue No.1 in the Affirmative 17. Issue No.2:

The respondent No.1 has contended that the owner of the offending vehicle violated the terms and condition of the insurance policy, as the offending vehicle was not authorized to ply on the road where the accident occurred.
It was specifically alleged that the offending vehicle did not have a valid route permit to operate on Bannerghatta Road, where the accident took place.

On this ground, the respondent No.1 claims that it is not liable to indemnify the owner and is, therefore ,
absolved liability to pay compensation to the petitioners.
18. To substantiate this contention, the RTO Bengaluru central, was examined as RW1.

He produced route permit at EX R5. and stated that the permit allowed the offending vehicle to operate between Honnahalli and Bengaluru via Sompura, Akkirampura, Kottigere, Dabaspet, Thamanagondalu,
Byarashettihalli, Nelamangala, Tavarekere.

During the cross-examination, he admitted that deviation from the permitted route may occur in certain circumstances, such as ongoing metro or road construction but also clarified that prior permission from traffic police is necessary for such Jaishankar vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67611318/
4 deviation.
19.

entities.text: Jaishankar vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: RW2 has stated that the offending vehicle was plying on Bannerghatta road, for which it had no route permit, thus amounting to a breach of policy conditions.
The testimony of RW1 supported the contention of the respondent-insurance company that the offending vehicle was operating outside its authorized route at time of the accident.

20. The Respondent no 1 has relied upon the decision rendered in MFA No 967/2017 between Sri Venkatesh V IFFCO TOKIO GEN-INSURANCE CO LTD and others, Judgment dated 22-4-2022 wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has held that there was no permit to ply the bus at the spot of the accident.
Based on evidence and record the tribunal has rightly absolved the insurer and directed the owner of the offending vehicle to satisfy the award.

21. The petitioners have relied upon the following decisions:
1. ILR 1991 KAR 4127 - K.V.Thimmegowda Vs. Kamalammam, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held that An insurance company is liable to pay compensation in respect of the injury or death of a third party, caused by a motor accident by a motor vehicle, which is a stage carriage while plying or being used lawfully otherwise than as a stage carriage, at a public place, even if such public place does not lie on the route in respect of which it is permitted to operate as a stage carriage.
2. MFA.10430/2012 - LRs of M.R.Basavanthappa Vs. Smt.Mallamma and others,
Judgment dated 23-2-2024, wherein Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has given same view of K.V.Thimmegowda Vs. Kamalamma.

entities.text: MFA.10430/2012 - LRs of M.R.Basavanthappa Vs. Smt.Mallamma and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 22. Keeping in view of above said decisions, I have once again perused the material available on record.

The charge sheet has been filed against the owner of the offending vehicle for the offence under section 66(1) R/w 192(a) IMV Act alleging that the offending vehicle was plying on Bannerghatta road, for which it had no route permit.
On perusal of Ex.R.7 - policy and Ex.R.5 - 'route permit, it is established that as on the date of alleged accident, the offending vehicle was covered by a valid and road permit.
In the present case on hand, there is no dispute regarding with regard to validity of policy and permit.
Only dispute pertains to whether the offending vehicle had the requisite permit to ply on the alleged road at the alleged place of accident.

23. The petitioners have contended that the because of ongoing metro or road construction, the offending vehicle was compelled to deviate from its permitted route due to ongoing metro and road construction .
However, no material evidence has been produced to substantiate this claim.

On the other hand, RW1-RTO has stated that the route permit granted to the the offending allowed it to operate between Honnahalli and Bengaluru via Sompura, Akkirampura, Kottigere, Dabaspet,
Thamanagondalu, Byarashettihalli, Nelamangala, Tavarekere.
It is evident from the record that the offending vehicle was plying on Bannerghatta road at time of accident, for which it had no route permit.

Neither the owner nor the driver of the offending vehicle has contested the case or produced Jaishankar vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67611318/
5 any documentary evidence to establish that due to ongoing metro and road construction or offending vehicle was authorized to operate on the said road.

entities.text: Jaishankar vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Therefore, in the absence of rebuttal and in light of the evidence on record, the contention raised by the respondent no 1- insurance company stands substantiated, and it is held that the offending vehicle was indeed operating outside its authorized route.
24.
Whether unauthorized deviation from the approved route constitutes a breach of the terms of the insurance policy.

In the light recent decision relied upon by the petitioner, this tribunal is of the considered opinion that such deviation, by itself, does not absolve the insurer from its liability to pay compensation.
Therefore, the insurer cannot be exempted from its obligation under the policy merely on the ground of unauthorized route deviation.
Hence, I answer issue no.2 in the Negative.
25. ISSUE NO.3:- Petitioners states that they are the legal heirs of the deceased Selvi.
The Petitioner No.1 to 3, the husband, two daughters of the deceased.

They have produced the Aadhaar cards of Petitioners and deceased at Ex.P.10 to 13 and the family ration card at Ex.P.14, which clearly indicates that deceased was the wife of first Petitioner and the Petitioner No.2 and 3 are the children of the deceased Selvi.
Hence, I hold that the Petitioners are the legal representatives of the deceased.
Therefore, petitioners are entitled for compensation as dependents.
26. It is stated that the deceased was 49 years old and was working as a Tailor and was earning .25,000/- P.M. and the sole earning member of the family.

To prove the occupation and income,
the Petitioners have not produced any documents.
In the absence of proof of income, this tribunal is of the opinion that the notional income to be assessed as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority.
Since the accident has been occurred in the year 2023, notional income Rs.16,000/- per month is taken for the assessment of compensation.

27. The PW-1 has produced Ex.P.13-Aadhaar card of deceased, which shows the year of birth of deceased as 1974 and considering the same, she was aged 49 years as on the date of accident and proper multiplier applicable to the case is 13.

As the age of the deceased was aged 49 years, 25%
future prospects is to be added as per Pranay Sethi case.
Then the monthly income would be .16,000+25%=.20,000/-.

As there are 3 dependents, as per the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 1/3rd of the income to be deducted towards her personal and living expenses and then the annual income would come around (Rs.13,334 X 12) Rs.1,60,008/- and applying 13 multiplier, Petitioners are awarded Rs.20,80,104/- towards loss of dependency.

entities.text: Sarla Verma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation reported in 2009 ACJ 1298
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 28. CONSORTIUM:

By following the guidelines of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs- Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram & Others., this Tribunal deems it proper to hold that the Petitioners are entitled .44,000/- each under the head of consortium as Petitioner No.1 has lost his wife, Petitioner No.2 and 3 have lost their mother.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs- Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram & Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 29. Loss to estate:
It appears that the Petitioner No.1 has lost his wife and the daughters have lost their mother.
Hence, .20,000/- is awarded towards loss to estate.

6

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 30. Funeral Expenses:
Petitioners have claimed that they have spent .2,00,000/- towards transportation of dead body, funeral & obsequies ceremony expenses.
By considering the facts and circumstances it would be proper to award .16,500/- for the funeral and other incidental expenses.

31. In all, the amount of compensation awarded by this Tribunal to the Petitioner under various headings is as follows :
Sl.No Nature of Compensation Amount 1. Loss of dependency . 20,80,104/-
2. Loss of consortium . 1,32,000/-
3. Loss to estate . 20,000/-
4. Transportation of .

16,500/-
dead body, Funeral & obsequies Expenses Total .
As I have discussed in detail under issue no 2 that deviation from the approved route does not, by itself, absolve the insurer from its liability to pay compensation.
Therefore, the insurer cannot be exempted from its obligation under the policy solely on the ground of unauthorized route deviation.
33. In the present case, the Petitioner has adduced cogent and reliable evidence to establish that the accident has occurred due to the rash or negligent driving of driver of offending vehicle.
It is also undisputed that the insurance policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Accordingly, the Respondent No.1 and 2 being the insurer and insured of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
However, in view of the issuance policy, the Respondent No.1 is held liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner with interest at 6% per annum.
With these observations, I have answered Issue No.3 partly in the Affirmative.
34. ISSUE NO.4 :

In view of the above discussion, reasons stated and findings given to Issue Nos. 1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Petition filed under Sec.166 of M.V. Act is allowed in part with cost.
Petitioners are awarded compensation of .22,48,604/- together with interest @ 6%
p.a. from the date of petition till the realization.
Respondent No.1 shall deposit the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.

After deposit of amount, 50% of the amount is apportioned to 1st Petitioner and 25% each to the Petitioner No.2 and Jaishankar vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67611318/
7 3.

Advocate's fee is fixed at .1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
